property_summary: For any caller and any value sent to Put, the reference contract never allows reentrant execution of Put during its execution (so a reentrant attacker cannot increase its recorded Acc[msg.sender].balance twice within one external Put call); the mutant omitting locked_ = true allows reentrant Put to run and change the post-Put stored balance, breaking this property for some inputs.

After any single external Put call made by an EOA, the stored Acc[caller].balance increases exactly by the msg.value (no additional change via reentrant Put); the mutant that omits setting locked_ = true allows a reentrant attacker to cause Acc[caller].balance to grow by more than msg.value during that same Put, violating the rule for some inputs.

For any caller and any single external Put call, the contract's stored Acc[caller].balance increases by exactly msg.value (no more) because nonReentrant_ prevents reentrant Put; the mutant that omits setting locked_ = true allows a reentrant attacker to reenter Put and cause the stored balance to grow by more than msg.value for some inputs.

For any single external Put call invoked by a contract that reenters via its receive/fallback, the reference C ensures the final stored Acc[caller].balance increases by exactly the single msg.value (reentrant calls are blocked); the mutant omitting locked_ = true allows the attacker to reenter and make Acc[caller].balance grow by more than msg.value for some fuzzed inputs.

For any caller and any single external Put call, the reference contract ensures the caller's recorded Acc[caller].balance increases by exactly the sent msg.value (no extra increments due to reentrancy); the mutant that omits setting locked_ = true in the nonReentrant_ modifier allows a reentrant attacker to cause Acc[caller].balance to increase by more than msg.value for some inputs.

For any caller and any sent value and unlockTime, the correct contract ensures acc.unlockTime is never set to a time earlier than the current block.timestamp (Put clamps unlockTime to >= block.timestamp); the mutant can set acc.unlockTime < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime, violating this invariant.

For any caller, after calling Put(x) the stored Acc[caller].unlockTime is always >= block.timestamp in the reference (it clamps to now), but the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = x can set it < block.timestamp for some fuzzed x, violating this invariant.

For any caller and any inputs, after Put(...) completes the stored Acc[caller].unlockTime is always >= the block.timestamp (reference clamps to now); the mutant that assigns unlockTime directly can make Acc[caller].unlockTime < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime, breaking this invariant.

For any caller and any sent value, after calling Put(_unlockTime) the reference contract always sets Acc[caller].unlockTime to be at least the previous stored unlockTime (it never decreases the stored unlockTime), while the mutant can decrease Acc[caller].unlockTime by assigning the provided _unlockTime directly, so there exist fuzzed inputs that make Acc[caller].unlockTime smaller than before the call.

For any caller and any _unlockTime, calling Put(_unlockTime) on the correct contract never sets the stored Acc[caller].unlockTime to a value smaller than the maximum of its previous unlockTime and block.timestamp; the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can decrease the stored unlockTime below that bound for some fuzzed inputs.

For any caller and any amount that meets the withdrawal conditions, the reference contract always forwards the full requested ETH outcall without reverting but only deducts the account balance when that external call returns success; replacing the call with transfer (2300 gas) can cause the external transfer to revert for a contract receiver, causing Collect to revert and so the observable success/failure behavior differs (the reference returns success while the mutant may revert).

For any caller, amount, and unlock time where the holder has sufficient balance and unlock time passed, the reference contract's Collect call never reverts when the callee's fallback may revert (it uses low-level call and handles failure), whereas the mutant using payable(...).transfer will revert for a callee that reverts on receiving ether; thus the reference always returns success while the mutant can fail for some inputs.

For any caller, amount and unlockTime where the holder has at least MinSum and amount and the unlockTime has passed, the reference C always returns successfully from Collect (it does not revert) even if the recipient's fallback reverts because it uses a low-level call and checks its return, whereas the mutant using payable(...).transfer can revert when the recipient reverts on receive; thus the rule: Collect(...) does not revert for any admissible inputs — the mutant violates this for some inputs.

For any caller with an on-chain contract receiver that has a payable fallback which reverts, the reference C never reverts from Collect(...) when the holder has sufficient balance and unlockTime passed (it performs a low-level call and tolerates failure), whereas the mutant using payable(...).transfer will revert when the recipient reverts; therefore: for any admissible (actor contract, amount, unlockTime) where Acc[actor].balance >= MinSum & >= amount and unlockTime passed, calling Collect by that actor always returns (does not revert) on the reference but may revert on the mutant.

For any actor with sufficient balance and passed unlockTime, calling Collect on the reference contract never reverts even if the recipient reverts on receive (the reference tolerates failing external sends via low-level call), whereas the mutant using payable(...).transfer can revert for some recipient contracts that revert on receive.

Reference contract C enforces non-reentrancy on Collect so that an attacker cannot withdraw more than the depositor's balance in a single Collect invocation; the mutant that clears locked_ before the external call allows reentrancy and can withdraw extra funds, violating this invariant.

For any depositor and withdraw amount, after a successful Collect call the contract's recorded balance for that depositor is reduced by exactly the withdrawn amount; the mutant that clears locked_ before the external call allows a reentrant attacker to drain extra funds so this invariant can be violated.

For any depositor and withdraw amount, after calling Collect the contract's reported holder balance never increases (i.e., new balance <= old balance); the mutant enabling reentrancy can cause the holder's recorded balance to end up higher than before (by reentrant interleaving), violating this monotonic non-increase property.

For any depositor and withdraw amount, if Collect succeeds (does not revert) then the contract's recorded depositor balance after the call equals the prior balance minus the withdrawn amount; the mutant that clears locked_ before the external call allows a reentrant attacker to withdraw extra funds so this equality can be violated for some inputs.

For any depositor and withdraw amount where Collect returns successfully, the depositor's recorded balance decreases by exactly the withdrawn amount (i.e., postBalance = preBalance - amount); the mutant that clears locked_ before the external call allows a reentrant attacker to make Collect succeed while draining more than amount, violating this equality for some inputs.

For any caller and amount, Collect may only succeed when block.timestamp is strictly greater than the holder's unlockTime; the mutant that uses >= allows collection when timestamp == unlockTime, which can make Collect succeed earlier.

For all actors, amounts and unlockTimes, Collect can only succeed when block.timestamp > stored unlockTime (strictly greater); the mutant using >= allows Collect to succeed when block.timestamp == unlockTime, violating this strict-inequality invariant.

For every caller, amount and unlockTime, the reference contract only allows Collect to succeed when block.timestamp is strictly greater than the stored unlockTime; the mutant changed > to >= so it can succeed when block.timestamp == unlockTime, violating that strict-timestamp rule.

For any depositor, if they attempt to Collect an amount _am equal to their entire stored balance at exactly the stored unlockTime, the reference contract MUST NOT transfer funds (Collect must fail), whereas the mutant (using >=) can succeed and transfer funds at timestamp == unlockTime.

For every depositor and amount, the reference contract never allows Collect to succeed at block.timestamp == acc.unlockTime (requires strictly greater), while the mutant using >= can succeed at that exact timestamp for some inputs, so the test checks that Collect reverts (or returns false) when called exactly at unlockTime.
